structured_output.what_is_happening: This is a token launched directly on PumpSwap, not through the pump.fun curve. Its name is "51吃瓜网官方首发Meme", roughly "the 51 Chigua (Chinese gossip site) official first-launch meme". It is 14 minutes old and worth about $30k. In its first 15 minutes it had heavy buying: about 1,177 unique buyers against 52 sellers, $260k volume and a +100–156% price move. The packet lists at least 10 earlier tokens with the exact same name and ticker, all created in the past roughly 19 hours. Every one now shows about $0 liquidity with absurd leftover market caps, which is what a pulled pool looks like. The most recent (4PRYX..., about 2 hours old) did $392k of hourly volume and still went to zero liquidity. This coin has the same setup: the creator put in the liquidity alone and none of it is locked (100% unlocked, a RugCheck danger flag), the creator holds 19% of supply, and there is no website, socials or DexScreener profile, only an X handle, "gua51x".

narrative.description: A Chinese-language meme tied to 51吃瓜网, a well-known Chinese gossip/scandal website, and claiming to be its 'official first launch'. The appeal is aimed at Chinese-speaking retail traders.
narrative.why_spreading: The 'official' claim draws Chinese-speaking retail traders, which fits the lopsided buyer/seller counts. But the same name has been relaunched 10+ times in a day and each copy died. This looks like a repeated scam template, not a story that is building.

token_connection.why_this_token: It is the only live pool under this name right now, with about $37k liquidity. Nothing on-chain or in the packet ties it to the real 51吃瓜网 site; the only link is an unverified X handle.
token_connection.competing_tokens: At least 10 tokens with the same name and ticker 51X from the past ~19 hours, all with about $0 liquidity (pulled). The latest, 4PRYX..., did $392k of hourly volume before dying.

authenticity.evidence: The same name was relaunched serially and every earlier copy's liquidity was pulled. The creator seeded unlocked liquidity alone and keeps 19% of supply. Buyers outnumber sellers about 23 to 1, which fits a pool being filled before the liquidity is pulled. No website, socials or DexScreener profile.
authenticity.uncertainty: The GMGN creator wallet shows no other launches, so the copies may come from different deployers or from copycats. The 1,177 buyers may be real Chinese retail. Bot/degen rate is 0 and there are no bundler or sniper wallets.

structural_risks: 100% of the LP is unlocked and the creator can remove it at any time
Creator holds 18.99% of supply (GMGN also flags this wallet as a rat trader)
10+ earlier copies of this exact name all ended with liquidity pulled
Only a few liquidity providers, so the pool is controlled by one party
No socials or site, so there is no community base

structured_output.counterargument: The buying is broad: about 1,177 unique buyers, 0% bot rate, no bundlers or snipers. It launched outside the pump.fun curve with $37k of liquidity, more than its market cap. If the creator is a legitimate team, or chooses to farm fees and push the price up before exiting, going from $32k to $64k only takes a modest amount of further buying from Chinese-speaking traders. The earlier copies may have been clones made by others, which would make this one the "real" launch.
unknowns: Whether this creator is behind the earlier same-name copies
Whether the X handle gua51x is really connected to 51吃瓜网
Who is buying (a Chinese community or recycled wallets)
Whether the creator will remove liquidity or sell the 19% into buyers

structured_output.thesis: This looks like a repeated liquidity-pull scam. One party holds the pool with no lock, the creator keeps 19% of supply, and 10+ identical-name tokens were all pulled within the past day. Heavy one-sided buying is the usual fill-up before the pull. A take-profit at 2x is possible but much less likely than losing the whole position to a liquidity pull.
